definition_zh: 商标；注册商标；商标专用权；标志性特征
definition_en: a name, symbol, or design registered by a business to identify its goods and set them apart from those of others
core_image: 一只木桶上烙下的记号：买家凭这个印记认出这是谁家的货
scene: 展会上，一家老牌食品厂的展台上挂着熟悉的红白标识，客户一眼就认出了它。The red and white symbol on the booth was a trademark that customers recognized at once.
sceneCN: 这里 trademark 是「商标」（第 1 个义项：标明商品来源的名称、符号或图案）；句意：展台上那个红白标识是顾客一眼就能认出的商标。

pos.zh: 商标；注册商标；标志性特征

collocations.zh: 商标淡化；削弱商标显著性

derivatives.zh: 由 trademark 加 -ed 构成，义为「已注册为商标的；带商标标识的」
由 trademark 加 -ing 构成，义为「商标注册；商标申请行为」
由 trademark 加 -able 构成，义为「可以注册为商标的」

senses.title: A mark that identifies goods
senses.definition: a name, symbol, or design that a trader registers to identify goods and set them apart from rival products
senses.definitionCN: 经营者注册用来标明商品来源、区分同类商品的名称、符号或图案
senses.example: The company put its trademark on every box it shipped.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把商标印在每一个发出去的盒子上。
senses.why: Trade supplies the market and mark supplies the visible sign, so the compound names the sign that carries a business reputation.
senses.whyCN: trade 提供市场，mark 提供可见的记号，复合词指承载商家信誉的那个记号。

senses.title: The exclusive legal right
senses.titleCN: 商标专用权；注册商标权
senses.definition: the exclusive right that registration gives an owner to use the mark and to stop others from using it
senses.definitionCN: 注册赋予权利人的专用权，可以自己使用并阻止他人使用
senses.example: Registration gave the firm a trademark good for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 注册使这家公司获得为期十年的商标权。
senses.why: Once a mark is registered it stops being a mere sign and becomes a piece of property that a court can enforce.
senses.whyCN: 商标一经注册就不再只是记号，而成为可以在法院主张的财产。

senses.title: A recognized brand sign
senses.definition: the mark seen as the public face of a product, the sign by which buyers know a brand
senses.definitionCN: 作为产品公众形象的标识，买家凭它认出某个品牌
senses.example: That curved bottle is the trademark of the whole industry.
senses.exampleCN: 那个弧形瓶是整个行业的招牌标识。
senses.why: A mark works only when buyers remember it, so the noun also names the recognizable identity itself.
senses.whyCN: 记号只有在买家记得住时才起作用，所以这个词也指那个可被认出的身份本身。

senses.title: A personal hallmark
senses.definition: a habit, feature, or style that makes a person or thing instantly recognizable
senses.definitionCN: 让人或物一眼可辨的习惯、特征或风格
senses.example: Slowing down to greet the doorman was his trademark.
senses.exampleCN: 放慢脚步跟门卫打招呼，是他的招牌做派。
senses.why: A legal mark and a personal habit both stamp a sign on what they touch, so the word spreads to human style.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的商标与个人习惯都是把印记盖在所及之物上，于是这个词扩展到人的风格。

senses.title: The printed TM or R symbol
senses.definition: the small symbol printed beside a name to show a trademark claim or a completed registration
senses.definitionCN: 印在名称旁边的小符号，表示商标主张或已完成注册
senses.example: The tiny letters after the name show it is an unregistered trademark.
senses.exampleCN: 名称后面那几个小字母表示它是一件未注册商标。
senses.why: Traders needed a compact sign on the label, so the noun came to name the symbol itself.
senses.whyCN: 商家需要在标签上有一个简短的标记，于是这个名词也指符号本身。

senses.title: A mark gone generic
senses.definition: a former trademark that the public now uses as the ordinary name of the product
senses.definitionCN: 原为商标、如今被公众当作产品通称使用的名称
senses.example: The word escalator began as a trademark and ended as a common noun.
senses.exampleCN: escalator 一词起初是商标，最后成了普通名词。
senses.why: When a mark succeeds too well, buyers use it as the product name, and the law then withdraws protection.
senses.whyCN: 商标成功过头，买家把它当成产品名称，法律便收回保护。

intro.en: Trademark is a transparent English compound of trade, the business of buying and selling, and mark, a visible sign stamped on goods.
intro.cn: trademark 是透明的英语复合词：trade（买卖）加 mark（打或印在货物上的可见记号）。

items.en: The reconstructed root merg- means a boundary or border mark.
items.cn: 重构词根 merg- 意为边界或界标。

items.en: Mearc means a boundary, a sign, or a landmark.
items.cn: mearc 意为边界、记号或地标。

items.en: Trade means a track or course, and later a regular course of business.
items.cn: trade 意为路径、轨道，后来指固定的营业行道。

items.en: Trade and mark meet in the market, where a mark on goods shows whose goods they are.
items.cn: trade 与 mark 在市场里相遇：货物上的记号说明货物归谁。

items.en: Trademark becomes one word as registration statutes turn marks into assets.
items.cn: 随着注册成文法把记号变成资产，trademark 合成一个词。

items.en: Trademark now covers brand identity, licensing, and dilution actions.
items.cn: trademark 如今涵盖品牌识别、许可使用与商标淡化诉讼。

note.en: Trademark sits beside trade name, service mark, and the ordinary words brand and logo.
note.cn: trademark 与 trade name、service mark 以及普通的 brand、logo 相邻。

entries.definition: the name under which a business trades, protected separately from a mark
entries.definitionCN: 商号；营业名称，与商标分开保护

entries.definition: a mark that identifies a service rather than goods
entries.definitionCN: 服务商标，标明服务而非商品来源

entries.definition: an official stamp struck on gold or silver to certify its purity
entries.definitionCN: 金银器上的官方成色印记；同样含 mark，指打在器皿上的记号

entries.definition: a name or design that identifies a product in the market
entries.definitionCN: 品牌；商品的名称与形象

entries.definition: the graphic element of a mark
entries.definitionCN: 标识图案；徽标

entries.definition: the tag on goods that carries the maker name
entries.definitionCN: 标签；货签

normalIntro.en: Trademark is built from two everyday words, so it can be read as a sign of trade.
normalIntro.cn: trademark 由两个日常词构成，可以直接读作「买卖的记号」。

normal.en: Trade is the business of buying and selling.
normal.cn: trade 就是买卖的行当。

normal.en: A mark is any sign you can see.
normal.cn: mark 就是任何看得见的记号。

normal.en: Together they name the sign that tells buyers whose goods these are.
normal.cn: 合起来，它指告诉买家货是谁家的那个记号。

normal.en: Register a trademark and the sign becomes property.
normal.cn: register a trademark 之后，记号就成了财产。

normal.en: Trademark infringement is copying that sign.
normal.cn: trademark infringement 就是照抄那个记号。

abstract.en: Picture a hot iron stamping a barrel in a warehouse.
abstract.cn: 想象烧红的烙铁在仓库里给木桶烙印。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate on the wall that turns that stamp into a title deed.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一张证书，把那个烙印变成地契。

abstract.en: Picture buyers in a street pointing at one sign and saying that is the one.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的买家指着某个标识说，就是它家。

examples.en: The startup registered its trademark before the launch.
examples.cn: 这家初创公司在产品发布前注册了商标。

examples.en: Copying a rival trademark can lead to a lawsuit.
examples.cn: 抄袭对手的商标可能招来诉讼。

examples.en: That blue box has become the trademark of the brand.
examples.cn: 那个蓝盒子已经成了该品牌的招牌标识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trade 加 mark」读起来像「吹得马克」——把牌子吹得响亮，让顾客记住这个记号；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 trade（买卖）加 mark（记号）：中世纪商人把记号烙在木桶与货箱上，买家凭记号认货；这个记号后来由注册制度变成财产，核心义是「买卖的记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Trademark starts as the visible sign on goods, then becomes the registered right, the recognized brand, a personal hallmark, the printed symbol, and finally a mark that has gone generic.
sensesIntro.cn: trademark 从货物上的可见记号出发，进而指注册取得的专用权、被认出的品牌、个人的招牌做派、印在名称旁的符号，最后指沦为通称的商标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark burned onto a barrel so buyers know whose goods they are.
core.cn: 核心意象：烙在木桶上的记号，让买家知道货是谁家的。

branches.en: The visible sign on goods is the first sense.
branches.cn: 货物上的可见记号是第一义项。

branches.en: Registration turns the sign into an exclusive right.
branches.cn: 注册把记号变成专用权。

branches.en: The famous mark becomes the public face of a brand.
branches.cn: 知名标识成为品牌对外的门面。

branches.en: A personal habit borrows the stamping image.
branches.cn: 个人习惯借用了「打记号」的意象。

branches.en: The printed symbol and the generic name mark the two ends of a mark life.
branches.cn: 印在标签上的符号与沦为通称的名称，标志着一个商标生命的两个端点。

intro.en: Trademark is a transparent English compound; its parts are trade and mark, with a small family of verb and adjective forms built on it.
intro.cn: trademark 是透明的英语复合词，由 trade 与 mark 构成，并带出一小族动词与形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: trade comes from Middle Low German and mark from Old English, while medieval Latin marca merely echoes the same Germanic sign.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：trade 来自中古低地德语，mark 来自古英语，只有中世纪拉丁语 marca 与「记号」呼应。

items.meaning: commerce, the business of buying and selling
items.example: Trade supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: trade 提供复合词的前半。

items.example: Mark supplies the visible half.
items.exampleCN: mark 提供可见的那一半。

items.example: The root is written with a star to show reconstruction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根通常加星号，表示它是重构形式。

items.example: Mearc is the Old English ancestor of mark.
items.exampleCN: mearc 是 mark 的古英语祖形。

items.example: The German word gives English trade its course sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个德语词给英语 trade 带来「路径」义。

items.example: Medieval Latin marca records the same Germanic sign.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 marca 记录了同一个日耳曼记号。

items.example: The compound joins the two halves into one word.
items.exampleCN: 复合词把两半合成一个词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms trademarked.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 trademarked。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms trademarking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 trademarking。

items.example: The suffix -able forms trademarkable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 trademarkable。

definition_zh: 专利；专利证书；专利权；取得专利；明显的；受专利保护的
definition_en: an exclusive right granted by the state for an invention, or, as an adjective, lying open and therefore clearly visible
core_image: 一只敞开的木匣：图纸摊在众人眼前，独占的许可只交到发明人手上
scene: 小作坊里，老师傅把新做的齿轮装置画成图纸，报给官府，换回一张盖了印的文书。The old workshop filed drawings of its new gear device and came back with a patent.
sceneCN: 这里 patent 是「专利证书」（第 2 个义项：载明独占权的官方文书）；句意：老作坊把新齿轮装置的图纸报了上去，换回一张专利证书。

pos.zh: 明显的；专利的；受专利保护的

derivatives.zh: 由 patent 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地；公然地」
由 patent 加 -ee 构成，义为「专利权人」
由 patent 加 -able 构成，义为「可取得专利的」
由 patentable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可专利性」

senses.title: An exclusive right in an invention
senses.definition: a right given by the state that lets an inventor stop others from making or selling the invention for a set term
senses.definitionCN: 国家授予发明人的权利，可在一定期限内阻止他人制造或销售该发明
senses.example: The lab holds a patent on the cooling method.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室拥有那项冷却方法的专利。
senses.why: Letters patent were open documents by which a ruler granted a privilege, and the invention right inherited that grant.
senses.whyCN: letters patent 是君主授予特权的公开文书，发明权继承了这种「授予」的结构。

senses.title: The document itself
senses.definition: the published document that describes the invention and states the right
senses.definitionCN: 公开描述发明并载明权利的文书
senses.example: The engineer read every page of the patent before designing around it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师逐页读完那份专利，再设法绕开它。
senses.why: The grant was a written instrument, so the paper and the right ended up sharing one name.
senses.whyCN: 授予行为落实为书面文书，于是文书与权利共用一个名称。

senses.title: The protected invention
senses.titleCN: 专利技术；受保护的发明
senses.definition: the technical solution that the document protects, seen as a piece of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 受文书保护的技术方案，被当作一项知识成果
senses.example: The new patent covers a cheaper way to coat glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新专利涵盖一种更便宜的玻璃镀膜方法。
senses.why: Buyers and rivals say the patent when they mean the technology inside it.
senses.whyCN: 买家与对手说「那项专利」时，指的其实是里面的技术。

senses.title: To obtain a patent
senses.definition: to secure a patent for an invention by filing and prosecuting an application
senses.definitionCN: 通过提交并推进申请，为一项发明取得专利
senses.example: They patented the hinge before any rival thought of it.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何对手想到之前，他们就把那个铰链申请了专利。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb as firms began to treat the grant as an action they perform.
senses.whyCN: 当企业开始把「获得授权」当作自己执行的动作，名词就转为动词。

senses.title: Openly evident
senses.definition: so clear that it needs no proof, as in a patent error or a patent lie
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到无需证明，如明显的错误或明显的谎言
senses.example: It was a patent absurdity to insure a ship already sunk.
senses.exampleCN: 给一艘已经沉没的船投保，是明显的荒谬。
senses.why: Patere means to lie open, and what lies open to every eye needs no argument.
senses.whyCN: patere 意为敞开着，对所有人敞开的东西不需要论证。

senses.title: Of or protected by a patent
senses.definition: used before a noun for things belonging to patent law or covered by a patent
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指属于专利法或受某项专利覆盖的
senses.example: Patent rules decide who may sell the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 专利规则决定谁可以销售这种药。
senses.why: As patents became a legal field, the word took on attributive duty and named whatever the field touches.
senses.whyCN: 专利成为法律领域后，这个词承担定语职责，指该领域涉及的一切。

senses.title: A proprietary medicine
senses.definition: a medicine sold under a maker name, historically under letters patent or a proprietary claim
senses.definitionCN: 以厂商名义出售的药品，历史上凭公开特许或专有主张销售
senses.example: Patent medicines were sold by travelling shows a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪前，成药由巡回推销的班子售卖。
senses.why: Early remedies carried royal letters patent, and the phrase patent medicine outlived the grant itself.
senses.whyCN: 早期药品带着王室特许状，patent medicine 这个说法比特许制度活得更久。

intro.en: Patent comes from Latin patere, to lie open, through the phrase litterae patentes, open letters that a ruler sent to be read by all.
intro.cn: patent 来自拉丁语 patere（敞开着），经 litterae patentes（供所有人阅读的公开文书）进入英语。

items.en: Patere means to lie open or to be exposed to view.
items.cn: patere 意为敞开着、显露在外。

items.en: Patens, its present participle, means open or uncovered.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 patens 意为敞开的、未遮盖的。

items.en: Litterae patentes are open letters, sealed yet readable by anyone.
items.cn: litterae patentes 是公开文书，盖了印却人人可读。

items.en: Patent carries the sense of open or evident into French.
items.cn: patent 带着「公开、明显」的含义进入法语。

items.en: Patent enters English meaning open or publicly visible.
items.cn: patent 进入英语时意为公开的、众目可见的。

items.en: The open grant of a privilege becomes the patent on an invention.
items.cn: 公开授予的特权演变为针对一项发明的专利权。

note.en: Patent belongs to a family of open and granted words, and it shares its field with copyright, trademark, and licence.
note.cn: patent 属于「公开」与「授予」的词族，并与 copyright、trademark、licence 同处一个法律义场。

entries.definition: in a way that is plainly clear
entries.definitionCN: 明显地；公然地

entries.definition: the person who owns a patent
entries.definitionCN: 专利权人

entries.definition: able to be protected by a patent
entries.definitionCN: 可取得专利的

entries.definition: the right over the copying of a work of authorship
entries.definitionCN: 著作权；版权，与专利权同属知识产权

entries.definition: the registered sign that identifies goods
entries.definitionCN: 商标，与专利并列的另一类工业产权

entries.definition: permission given to use a protected right
entries.definitionCN: 许可；许可证，常与专利许可搭配

normalIntro.en: Patent carries one image through all its senses: something laid open, either a public document or a fact anyone can see.
normalIntro.cn: patent 的各个义项共用一个意象：被摊开的东西，或是一份公开文书，或是一个人尽可见的事实。

normal.en: Patere is Latin for lying open, which is why letters patent were read aloud.
normal.cn: patere 在拉丁语里是「敞开着」，所以公开文书要当众宣读。

normal.en: A patent trades disclosure for a limited monopoly.
normal.cn: 专利用公开技术换一段有限期的独占。

normal.en: Apply for a patent and the office publishes the drawings.
normal.cn: apply for a patent 之后，专利局会把图纸公开。

normal.en: Patent infringement is making the protected invention without permission.
normal.cn: patent infringement 就是未经许可实施受保护的发明。

normal.en: Patently obvious means the same as plainly obvious.
normal.cn: patently obvious 与 plainly obvious 同义，都是「明摆着」。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler opening a chest in public and handing one inventor the key.
abstract.cn: 想象君主当众打开一只匣子，把钥匙只交给一位发明人。

abstract.en: Picture a registry page pinned open so any passer-by can read the drawing.
abstract.cn: 想象登记簿的一页被摊开钉住，路过的人都能读到图纸。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawn around a blueprint, with a date written on the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象在图纸四周拉起围栏，门口写着一个到期日。

examples.en: The company filed a patent for the new battery in three countries.
examples.cn: 这家公司为新型电池在三个国家申请了专利。

examples.en: The drug is still under patent, so cheap copies cannot be sold.
examples.cn: 这种药仍在专利保护期内，所以不能销售廉价的仿制品。

examples.en: His excuse was a patent lie that nobody in the room believed.
examples.cn: 他的借口是明显的谎言，屋里没人相信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「怕疼」——发明人怕技术被抄得心疼，赶紧去申请专利；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 patere（敞开着）→ 现在分词 patens（公开的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 litterae patentes（公开文书）→ 英语 patent，核心义是「公开授予的独占权」，形容词义「明显的」直接来自「敞开着」。

sensesIntro.en: Patent begins with the open grant and its paper, moves to the protected technology and the act of obtaining it, then splits into the adjective of open evidence and the narrow field uses.
sensesIntro.cn: patent 先指公开的授予行为与那份文书，再指受保护的技术与取得专利的动作，随后分出「明显」的形容词义与几个领域用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document laid open on a table, with one inventor holding a sealed permit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份摊在桌上的文书，只有一位发明人握着盖印的许可。

branches.en: The granted right is the legal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 被授予的权利是这个词的法律中心。

branches.en: The paper that records the grant is the documentary sense.
branches.cn: 记录授予的纸质文书是文献义项。

branches.en: The technology inside the paper is what engineers mean by the patent.
branches.cn: 文书里的技术，是工程师说「那项专利」时的所指。

branches.en: The verb of obtaining and the attributive field use both grow from the grant.
branches.cn: 取得专利的动词义与领域定语用法，都从「授予」长出来。

branches.en: Open evidence and the old proprietary medicine keep the original open sense.
branches.cn: 「明显」的公开证据义与旧的成药义，都保留了最初的「敞开」义。

intro.en: Patent is built on the Latin verb patere and its participle, then grows English branches through -ee, -able, and -ly.
intro.cn: patent 建立在拉丁语动词 patere 及其分词之上，再借 -ee、-able、-ly 长出英语的分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin patere means to lie open; patens means open, and litterae patentes means open letters.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 patere 意为敞开；patens 意为敞开的；litterae patentes 意为公开文书。

items.meaning: to lie open, to be exposed
items.example: Patere supplies the open image behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: patere 提供所有义项背后的「敞开」意象。

items.example: Patens is the participle that carries the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: patens 是承载形容词义的分词。

items.example: The phrase names the document a ruler sent to be read by all.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语指君主发出、供所有人阅读的文书。

items.example: Patent keeps the grant sense in law.
items.exampleCN: patent 在法律中保留「授予」义。

items.example: The verb names what inventors do.
items.exampleCN: 动词义指发明人所做的事。

items.example: The suffix -ee forms patentee.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ee 构成 patentee。

items.example: The suffix -able forms patentable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 patentable。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms patentability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 patentability。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms patently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 patently。

items.example: Letters patent keeps the medieval phrase in modern law.
items.exampleCN: letters patent 把中世纪的说法留在现代法律里。

definition_zh: 合并；吸收合并；并购交易；机构合并；融为一体
definition_en: the joining of two or more companies or organizations into a single one, usually with one of them surviving
core_image: 两条河汇成一条：原先的两道水痕消失，只剩一条更宽的河道
scene: 两家地方银行谈了半年，最后把招牌并成一块，只留一处柜台。After six months of talks, the two local banks signed a merger and kept one counter.
sceneCN: 这里 merger 是「合并」（第 1 个义项：两家或多家公司合成一家）；句意：谈了近半年后，两家地方银行签下合并协议，只保留一处柜台。

pos.zh: 合并；吸收合并；并购交易

collocations.zh: 合并控制；经营者集中审查

derivatives.zh: 由 merger 反推的动词原形，义为「合并；使融为一体」
由 merge 加 -ing 构成，义为「合并过程；融合」
由 post-（在……之后）加 merger 构成，义为「合并后的」
由 pre-（在……之前）加 merger 构成，义为「合并前的」

senses.title: Two firms becoming one
senses.definition: the joining of two or more companies into a single company
senses.definitionCN: 两家或多家公司合成为一个公司
senses.example: The merger created the largest bank in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并造就了该地区最大的银行。
senses.why: Mergere means to dip one thing into another until the outline disappears, which is exactly what two firms do when they become one.
senses.whyCN: mergere 意为把一物浸入另一物直到轮廓消失，这正是两家公司合为一家时的情形。

senses.title: Absorption into a survivor
senses.definition: a statutory form in which one company is absorbed into another that keeps its name and identity
senses.definitionCN: 一种法定形式：一家公司被并入另一家，存续方保留自己的名称与主体资格
senses.example: The small rival disappeared in a merger into the parent bank.
senses.exampleCN: 那家小对手在并入母行的合并中消失了。
senses.why: The sinking image sharpens into a legal rule: one body sinks into the other, and only the survivor remains visible.
senses.whyCN: 「沉入」的意象落实为法律规则：一方沉入另一方，只有存续方仍然可见。

senses.title: The deal itself
senses.definition: the transaction and its negotiations, as in merger talks or a merger agreement
senses.definitionCN: 指这笔交易及其谈判过程，如合并谈判或合并协议
senses.example: The board approved the merger after a long night of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会经过一整夜的谈判后批准了这桩合并案。
senses.why: Deal makers speak of a merger as an event with a price and a timetable, so the word names the transaction.
senses.whyCN: 做交易的人把合并说成有价格、有日程的事件，于是这个词也指那笔交易。

senses.title: Joining of institutions
senses.definition: the union of non-corporate bodies such as banks, firms, schools, or hospitals
senses.definitionCN: 银行、事务所、学校或医院等非公司实体的联合
senses.example: The merger of the two law firms doubled the patent team.
senses.exampleCN: 两家律所合并，使专利团队扩大了一倍。
senses.why: The corporate sense spread to any two bodies that pool their people and name.
senses.whyCN: 公司义扩展到任何两个把人员与名号合在一起的机构。

senses.title: A blending into one
senses.definition: a general blending of things, qualities, or interests into a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 事物、性质或利益融合成一个整体
senses.example: The merger of sound and image made the film feel new.
senses.exampleCN: 声音与画面的融合让这部影片显得新鲜。
senses.why: Once the outline of a thing sinks away, the word can describe any blending, not only a corporate one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事物的轮廓沉没不见，这个词就能描述任何融合，不只限于公司。

senses.title: A concentration under review
senses.definition: the competition-law event of combining firms that may lessen competition and must be cleared
senses.definitionCN: 竞争法上的合并事件：合并可能削弱竞争，须经审查批准
senses.example: The regulator blocked the merger on the ground that it would raise prices.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构以合并会推高价格为由阻止了它。
senses.why: Competition law looks at the same event through a different lens, asking whether the joined body is too strong.
senses.whyCN: 竞争法从另一个角度看待同一事件，问的是合并后的主体是否过于强大。

intro.en: Merger comes from Latin mergere, to dip or sink, through French, and the legal sense grew from the image of one body sinking into another.
intro.cn: merger 来自拉丁语 mergere（浸入、沉没），经法语进入英语；法律义正是从「一方沉入另一方」的意象长出来的。

items.en: Mergere means to dip something into liquid or to plunge it under.
items.cn: mergere 意为把某物浸入液体，或把它按到水下。

items.en: Submergere and emergere grow from the same verb, one sinking under and one rising out.
items.cn: submergere 与 emergere 出自同一个动词，一个沉下去，一个冒出来。

items.en: Merger means to sink or to plunge.
items.cn: merger 意为沉没、浸入。

items.en: In property law, merger names one estate sinking into a larger one.
items.cn: 在财产法中，merger 指一项权益并入更大的权益而消失。

items.en: Company law borrows the word for one firm absorbed by another.
items.cn: 公司法借用这个词，指一家公司被另一家吸收。

items.en: Merger extends to banks, professional firms, and competition review.
items.cn: merger 扩展到银行、专业事务所与竞争审查。

note.en: Merger is the noun of sinking together, close to its own verb merge and to the whole merger family, and near acquisition and consolidation in deal talk.
note.cn: merger 是「沉到一处」的名词，与自己的动词 merge 及整个词族相邻，在交易语境里又与 acquisition、consolidation 接近。

entries.definition: to join two things into one
entries.definitionCN: 合并；使合为一体

entries.definition: the process of joining together
entries.definitionCN: 合并过程；融合

entries.definition: to put under water or to sink below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 使沉入水中；淹没，同出 mergere 一词

entries.definition: the buying of one company by another
entries.definitionCN: 收购；取得另一家公司的控制权

entries.definition: the combining of firms into a new entity rather than one absorbing the other
entries.definitionCN: 新设合并：几家合并成新主体，而不是一方吸收另一方

entries.definition: the gaining of control over a company, often against its will
entries.definitionCN: 接管；收购控制权，常含非自愿意味

normalIntro.en: Merger keeps the picture of one thing sinking into another until only a single shape is left.
normalIntro.cn: merger 始终保留着一物沉入另一物、最后只剩一个轮廓的画面。

normal.en: Mergere is Latin for dipping or sinking.
normal.cn: mergere 在拉丁语里就是浸入、沉没。

normal.en: Submerge and emerge are its close relatives, sinking under and rising out.
normal.cn: submerge 与 emerge 是它的近亲，一个沉下去，一个冒出来。

normal.en: A merger agreement is the paper that records the joining.
normal.cn: merger agreement 就是记录这次合并的文件。

normal.en: Merger control asks whether the joined firm is too strong.
normal.cn: merger control 问的是合并后的企业是否过于强大。

normal.en: Compare consolidation: a merger usually leaves one survivor, consolidation builds a new one.
normal.cn: 对比 consolidation：merger 通常留下一个存续方，consolidation 则另立新主体。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and losing their separate banks.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流相遇，各自的水岸都消失了。

abstract.en: Picture one boat sinking into a larger hull until only the big hull shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小船沉进更大的船体，最后只剩大船露在水面。

abstract.en: Picture two signboards taken down and one wider board put up.
abstract.cn: 想象两块招牌被摘下，换上一块更宽的。

examples.en: The merger of the two airlines was cleared after a year of review.
examples.cn: 两家航空公司的合并经过一年审查后获得批准。

examples.en: Shareholders must approve the merger agreement before it binds.
examples.cn: 合并协议要具有约束力，须先经股东批准。

examples.en: The merger gave the group a stronger position in three markets.
examples.cn: 这次合并使集团在三个市场上取得更强的地位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「木汁儿」——两家公司的汁液倒进同一只桶里，就分不出彼此了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mergere（浸入、沉没）→ 法语 merger（沉没）→ 英吉利法语与英语 merger，核心义「一方沉入另一方」，在财产法里指权益并入而消失，在十九世纪公司法里定型为「合并」。

sensesIntro.en: Merger starts with the plain joining of two firms, narrows into the statutory absorption by a survivor, widens to the deal and to institutions, then reaches the general blending and the competition-law event.
sensesIntro.cn: merger 先从两家公司合成一家讲起，收窄为存续方吸收另一方的法定形式，再扩展到交易本身与各类机构，最后触及一般的融合与竞争法上的合并事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two streams joining, with the separate banks of each stream vanishing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条溪流汇合，各自的水岸随之消失。

branches.en: The plain corporate joining is the central sense.
branches.cn: 最朴素的公司合并是中心义项。

branches.en: Absorption keeps the sinking image in statutory form.
branches.cn: 吸收合并把「沉没」意象保留为法定形式。

branches.en: The deal sense treats the merger as a priced event.
branches.cn: 交易义把合并当作有定价的事件。

branches.en: Institutional unions extend the joining beyond companies.
branches.cn: 机构合并把这种联合扩展到公司之外。

branches.en: General blending and competition review are the two widest edges of the word.
branches.cn: 一般融合与竞争审查是这个词最宽的两个边缘。

intro.en: Merger is built on the Latin verb mergere, with sub- and e- siblings, plus English -er, -ing, pre-, and post-.
intro.cn: merger 建立在拉丁语动词 mergere 之上，同族有带 sub- 与 e- 的兄弟词，英语里再加 -er、-ing、pre-、post-。

latinIntro.en: Latin mergere means to dip or sink; submergere sinks something under, emergere lifts it out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mergere 意为浸入、沉没；submergere 把东西按到水下，emergere 让它冒出来。

items.meaning: to dip, to plunge, to sink
items.example: Mergere supplies the whole sinking image.
items.exampleCN: mergere 提供整个「沉没」意象。

items.example: The prefix sub- builds submergere and submerge.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 构成 submergere 与 submerge。

items.example: The prefix e- builds emergere and emerge.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 构成 emergere 与 emerge。

items.example: The suffix -er turns merge into merger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 merge 变成 merger。

items.example: The verb is the everyday partner of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词最日常的搭档。

items.example: The noun carries the corporate sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词承载公司义。

items.example: The gerund names the process rather than the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个动名词指过程而非事件。

items.example: The prefix pre- forms pre-merger.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 构成 pre-merger。

items.example: The prefix post- forms post-merger.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 post- 构成 post-merger。

items.example: The compound names the regulatory side of a merger.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指合并的监管一面。

definition_zh: 子公司；附属机构；辅助的；附属的；补充的
definition_en: a company controlled by another company, or, as an adjective, serving in a secondary or supporting role
core_image: 后备队列站在主力身后：不冲在最前，却随时补位
scene: 集团总部把新收购的小厂挂在自己名下，小厂另立法人，账目却并进总表。The group kept the small plant as a subsidiary with its own legal name and one consolidated balance sheet.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidiary 是「子公司」（第 1 个义项：由另一家公司控股、但仍是独立法人的公司）；句意：集团把那家小厂留作子公司，它有独立的法律名称，账目则合并进同一张总表。

pos.zh: 子公司；附属机构；下属单位
辅助的；附属的；补充的；次要的

derivatives.zh: 与 subsidiary 同出 subsidium，义为「补贴；补助金」，是同一词根的另一个分支
由 subsidy 加 -ize 构成，义为「补贴；资助」
由 subsidiary 加 -ity 构成，义为「辅助原则」，指上级只在必要时介入
由 subsidiary 加 -ly 构成，义为「辅助地；次要地」

senses.title: A company owned by another
senses.definition: a separate legal company whose controlling shares are held by a parent company
senses.definitionCN: 股权由母公司控制、但自身仍是独立法人的公司
senses.example: The bank set up a subsidiary in Hong Kong to hold the loans.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在香港设立了一家子公司来持有这些贷款。
senses.why: Subsidium was the reserve force kept behind the line, and a controlled company stands behind its parent in the same supporting position.
senses.whyCN: subsidium 是留在阵线后方的后备力量，受控公司正以同样的支援姿态站在母公司身后。

senses.title: A dependent organization
senses.definition: an organization that depends on a larger body, such as a branch school or a subsidiary hospital
senses.definitionCN: 依附于更大机构的组织，如附属学校、附属医院
senses.example: The museum runs a subsidiary in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆在老城区办了一个附属展馆。
senses.why: The reserve image does not require a company, so any dependent body can be called a subsidiary.
senses.whyCN: 「后备」意象并不限于公司，任何依附性机构都可以叫 subsidiary。

senses.title: Serving in a secondary role
senses.definition: having a less important role that supports something else
senses.definitionCN: 作用较次要、用于支持别的事物
senses.example: Price was a subsidiary reason for choosing that supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 价格是选择那家供应商的一个次要原因。
senses.why: so the adjective means supporting rather than central.
senses.whyCN: 站在阵线后方的东西是在支援前方，所以形容词义是「辅助的」而非核心的。

senses.title: Attached and subordinate
senses.definition: used before a noun for something attached to a main body and subject to it
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指附属于主体并受其支配的事物
senses.example: The subsidiary company files its own tax return.
senses.exampleCN: 这家附属公司自行申报纳税。
senses.why: The noun sense lends the adjective its legal edge, naming whatever hangs from a main entity.
senses.whyCN: 名词义给形容词带来法律色彩，指从属于主体的一切。

senses.title: Supplementary, not essential
senses.definition: added to support a main thing, as in a subsidiary ledger or subsidiary evidence
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主要事物之旁以示支持，如明细账或辅助证据
senses.example: The auditor checked the subsidiary ledger against the main account.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师把明细账与总账核对了一遍。
senses.why: A reserve is not the main army but it completes it, so the word also means supplementary.
senses.whyCN: 后备力量不是主力，却把主力补全，所以这个词也有「补充」义。

senses.title: The group of controlled companies
senses.definition: the whole set of controlled companies belonging to one parent, taken as a group
senses.definitionCN: 同一母公司旗下所有受控公司构成的整体
senses.example: The parent and its subsidiaries report as one group.
senses.exampleCN: 母公司与其子公司作为一个集团合并报告。
senses.why: In group accounting the plural names the collection, the ring of reserve units around one centre.
senses.whyCN: 在集团会计里，复数形式指这一整圈围绕一个中心的后备单位。

intro.en: Subsidiary comes from Latin subsidium, the reserve troops kept behind the battle line, through the adjective subsidiarius.
intro.cn: subsidiary 来自拉丁语 subsidium（留在战线后方的后备部队），经形容词 subsidiarius 进入英语。

items.en: Subsidium means the troops held in reserve behind the line.
items.cn: subsidium 意为留在阵线后方的后备部队。

items.en: The word is generally explained as sub-, under, plus sedere, to sit, a force sitting behind.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词由 sub-（在下）加 sedere（坐）构成，即坐在后方的一支力量。

items.en: Subsidiarius means serving as a reserve or as help.
items.cn: subsidiarius 意为充当后备或援助的。

items.en: Subsidium also means help or relief in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 在一般文献里，subsidium 也指援助、救助。

items.en: Subsidiary enters English as an adjective meaning auxiliary.
items.cn: subsidiary 进入英语时是形容词，意为辅助的。

items.en: Company law gives the word its corporate sense of a controlled firm.
items.cn: 公司法赋予这个词「受控公司」的企业义。

note.en: Subsidiary belongs to the reserve family of subsidium, and in business it stands beside affiliate, branch, and its opposite, the parent company.
note.cn: subsidiary 属于 subsidium 的「后备」词族，在商业语境里与 affiliate、branch 并列，并与反义的 parent company 相对。

entries.definition: money paid by a government to support a price or an industry
entries.definitionCN: 政府为支持价格或产业而支付的补助金，同出 subsidium

entries.definition: to support something with money
entries.definitionCN: 以资金补贴、资助

entries.definition: in a supporting or secondary way
entries.definitionCN: 辅助地；次要地

entries.definition: a company linked to another by ownership or agreement
entries.definitionCN: 关联公司；因股权或协议而与另一家公司相连

entries.definition: a local office of a firm, without separate legal identity
entries.definitionCN: 分公司；分支机构，本身不是独立法人

entries.definition: the company that controls a subsidiary
entries.definitionCN: 母公司；控制子公司的公司，与子公司相对

normalIntro.en: Subsidiary keeps the picture of reserve troops: they stand behind the front line, ready to help but never the centre of the battle.
normalIntro.cn: subsidiary 保留着后备部队的画面：站在前线之后，随时支援，却从不是战场的中心。

normal.en: Subsidium was the reserve force behind the line.
normal.cn: subsidium 就是阵线后方的后备力量。

normal.en: A subsidiary company stands behind its parent the way reserves stand behind the front.
normal.cn: 子公司站在母公司身后，正如后备军站在前线之后。

normal.en: A wholly owned subsidiary is one whose shares all belong to the parent.
normal.cn: wholly owned subsidiary 就是股份全归母公司所有的子公司。

normal.en: A subsidiary ledger supports the main account.
normal.cn: subsidiary ledger 是用来支持总账的明细账。

normal.en: Compare subsidy: both words come from reserve help, but one is money and one is a body.
normal.cn: 对比 subsidy：两词都出自「后备援助」，一个指钱，一个指机构。

abstract.en: Picture a second row of soldiers half a step behind the first.
abstract.cn: 想象第二排士兵站在第一排之后半步。

abstract.en: Picture a small office with its own doorplate but the same owner upstairs.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小办公室，有自己的门牌，楼上却是同一个东家。

abstract.en: Picture a footnote page pinned under the main page of a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告正文下面钉着一页附表。

examples.en: The group sold its subsidiary in Brazil last year.
examples.cn: 集团去年卖掉了在巴西的子公司。

examples.en: Each subsidiary keeps its own board and its own accounts.
examples.cn: 每家子公司都有自己的董事会和自己的账目。

examples.en: Cost was a subsidiary concern; reliability mattered more.
examples.cn: 成本只是次要考虑，可靠性更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆词联想：sub（在下）加 sid（坐）加 iary——坐在下面、随时补位的那一排，就是后备，也就是子公司；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 subsidium（留在阵线后方的后备部队，一般认为由 sub-「在下」加 sedere「坐」构成）→ 形容词 subsidiarius（后备的、辅助的）→ 英语 subsidiary，核心义「站在后面待命支援的一方」，故有「辅助的」与「子公司」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidiary begins with the controlled company, widens to any dependent body, then turns adjectival for auxiliary and attached things, adds the supplementary sense, and ends with the group of controlled companies.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidiary 先指受控公司，扩展到任何依附性机构，再转为形容词表示辅助与附属，又添出补充义，最后指整个子公司群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reserve line standing half a step behind the front, ready to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在前线之后半步的后备队列，随时可以补上。

branches.en: The controlled company is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 受控公司是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Any dependent body can wear the same name.
branches.cn: 任何依附性机构都能用同一个名称。

branches.en: The adjective of auxiliary role comes straight from the reserve image.
branches.cn: 「辅助」的形容词义直接来自后备意象。

branches.en: The attributive sense marks legal attachment to a main body.
branches.cn: 定语义标示对主体的法律隶属关系。

branches.en: Supplementary records and the whole subsidiary group are the two accounting edges.
branches.cn: 补充性的账册与整个子公司群，是这个词在会计上的两个边缘。

intro.en: Subsidiary is built from Latin subsidium and the adjective ending -arius, with English -ary, -ly, -ity, and the parallel noun subsidy.
intro.cn: subsidiary 由拉丁语 subsidium 加形容词词尾 -arius 构成，英语里再带出 -ary、-ly、-ity，并有平行的名词 subsidy。

latinIntro.en: Latin subsidium means the reserve kept behind the line; subsidiarius means serving as a reserve or help.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subsidium 意为留在阵线后方的后备队；subsidiarius 意为充当后备或援助的。

items.example: Subsidium supplies the reserve image.
items.exampleCN: subsidium 提供「后备」意象。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the force behind the line.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把这支力量放在阵线之后。

items.example: Sedere builds the picture of troops sitting in reserve.
items.exampleCN: sedere 构成后备部队「坐着待命」的画面。

items.example: Subsidiarius is the direct Latin adjective.
items.exampleCN: subsidiarius 是直接的拉丁语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms subsidiary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 subsidiary。

items.example: The noun carries the corporate sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词承载企业义。

items.example: Subsidy is the money branch of the same root.
items.exampleCN: subsidy 是同一词根的「钱」分支。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms subsidize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 subsidize。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms subsidiarity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 subsidiarity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms subsidiarily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 subsidiarily。

definition_zh: 反垄断的；反托拉斯的；维护竞争的
definition_en: relating to laws and policies that prevent firms from combining or acting in ways that reduce competition
core_image: 一只手按住正在合拢的两块巨石：不让它们并成一座挡住市场通道的墙
scene: 听证会上，监管人员翻着两家公司的合并方案，担心新公司会把整条街的生意都攥在手里。At the hearing the regulator went through the merger plan and worried that the new firm would hold the whole street as an antitrust problem.
sceneCN: 这里 antitrust 是「反垄断的」（第 1 个义项：规制限制竞争行为的法律与政策）；句意：听证会上监管人员审读合并方案，担心新公司独占整条街的生意，构成反垄断问题。

pos.zh: 反垄断的；反托拉斯的；维护竞争的

collocations.zh: 违反反垄断法；垄断行为

derivatives.zh: 由 trust 加 buster 构成的复合词，义为「反托拉斯者；主张拆分垄断的人」，与 antitrust 同属反垄断义场
由 trust 加 busting 构成的复合词，义为「反托拉斯行动；拆分垄断企业」，是 antitrust 政策的通俗说法
由 anti- 加 monopoly 构成的近义复合词，义为「反垄断的」，多见于东亚竞争法文献

senses.title: Against restrictive combinations
senses.titleCN: 反垄断的；反限制竞争的
senses.definition: relating to the body of law that forbids agreements and practices which restrain trade
senses.definitionCN: 指禁止限制贸易的协议与行为的法律体系
senses.example: Antitrust law forbids rivals from fixing prices together.
senses.exampleCN: 反垄断法禁止竞争对手串通定价。
senses.why: Anti- means against and trust meant a giant combination of firms, so the word names the law set against such combinations.
senses.whyCN: anti- 意为反对，trust 指企业巨头联合，于是这个词指针对这类联合而设的法律。

senses.title: Against the old industrial trusts
senses.definition: belonging to the historical campaign against the great industrial trusts of the late nineteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 属于十九世纪末针对大型工业托拉斯的那场运动
senses.example: The antitrust movement of that decade broke up several railway pools.
senses.exampleCN: 那个十年的反托拉斯运动拆散了几个铁路联营组织。
senses.why: The name was coined for a specific target, the trust, and it still carries that historical colour.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字是为一个具体靶子「托拉斯」造出来的，至今带着那段历史色彩。

senses.title: Of enforcement bodies and cases
senses.definition: used of the agencies, investigations, and proceedings that apply competition law
senses.definitionCN: 用于实施竞争法的机构、调查与程序
senses.example: The antitrust authorities cleared the deal with conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 反垄断执法机构附条件批准了这笔交易。
senses.why: Once a law exists, the word attaches to the machinery that enforces it, not only to the rule on paper.
senses.whyCN: 法律一旦存在，这个词就附着在实施它的机器上，而不只指纸面上的规则。

senses.title: Keeping markets competitive
senses.definition: describing measures whose effect is to preserve rivalry between firms
senses.definitionCN: 描述以维持企业间竞争为目的的措施
senses.example: The remedy was praised as a genuinely antitrust solution.
senses.exampleCN: 这一救济被称赞为真正维护竞争的方案。
senses.why: The word can describe an effect, not just a rule, because its purpose is open rivalry in the market.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能描述一种效果而不只是规则，因为它的目的是市场上的公开竞争。

senses.title: Of the competition-law field
senses.definition: belonging to the academic and professional field that studies competition law
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究竞争法的学术与专业领域
senses.example: She teaches an antitrust course in the law faculty.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法学院讲授一门反垄断法课程。
senses.why: A body of law with its own doctrine becomes a field, and the adjective then labels its courses and journals.
senses.whyCN: 一套有自己的学说的法律会成为一个领域，形容词便用来标注它的课程与刊物。

senses.title: Breaking a monopoly apart
senses.definition: relating to structural remedies that split a dominant firm into competing units
senses.definitionCN: 指把支配性企业拆成互相竞争的单元的结构性救济
senses.example: A structural antitrust order divided the network into two firms.
senses.exampleCN: 一项结构性的反垄断命令把该网络拆成两家公司。
senses.why: The strongest form of the remedy is to undo the combination itself, so the word can name a break-up order.
senses.whyCN: 最强的救济是撤销联合本身，因此这个词也能指拆分命令。

intro.en: Antitrust is a coined American compound of Greek anti, against, and trust, the word for a giant combination of firms.
intro.cn: antitrust 是美语里新造的复合词：希腊语前缀 anti（反对）加 trust（企业巨头联合）。

items.en: Anti means against or in place of.
items.cn: anti 意为反对、代替。

items.en: Anti- passes into Latin as a prefix of opposition and reaches English through it.
items.cn: anti- 作为表示反对的前缀进入拉丁语，再经此进入英语。

items.en: Traust means help, confidence, or firm support, and English trust descends from it.
items.cn: traust 意为援助、信心、稳固的依靠，英语 trust 由此而来。

items.en: Trust comes to name a great combination of firms under a single board.
items.cn: trust 转而指由单一董事会控制的庞大企业联合。

items.en: Antitrust is coined for the statute passed against such combinations that year.
items.cn: antitrust 一词为当年针对这类联合而通过的成文法而造。

items.en: Antitrust widens into the general name for competition law in many countries.
items.cn: antitrust 扩展为许多国家竞争法的通称。

note.en: Antitrust is one of a large anti- family and it shares its field with the old trust, with monopoly, and with the cartel.
note.cn: antitrust 是庞大的 anti- 词族中的一员，并与旧的 trust、monopoly 以及 cartel 同处一个义场。

entries.definition: relating to measures against goods sold below their normal value abroad
entries.definitionCN: 反倾销的；针对在境外低价销售的货物，同用 anti- 前缀

entries.definition: tending to reduce rivalry in a market
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于削弱市场竞争的，与 antitrust 常成对照

entries.definition: directed against monopoly
entries.definitionCN: 反垄断的，与 antitrust 近义的另一种构词

entries.definition: a large combination of firms run by one board
entries.definitionCN: 托拉斯；由单一董事会经营的庞大企业联合，正是 antitrust 要反对的对象

entries.definition: the exclusive control of a market by one seller
entries.definitionCN: 垄断；一家卖方对市场的独占控制

entries.definition: a group of firms that agree to limit competition between them
entries.definitionCN: 卡特尔；协议限制彼此竞争的企业集团

normalIntro.en: Antitrust reads literally as against the trust, so the word can be taken apart into its two parts at sight.
normalIntro.cn: antitrust 字面上就是「反对托拉斯」，一眼就能拆成两半来记。

normal.en: Anti- is the prefix of opposition.
normal.cn: anti- 就是表示「反对」的前缀。

normal.en: A trust was a giant combination of firms under one board.
normal.cn: trust 原是由单一董事会控制的庞大企业联合。

normal.en: Put together, antitrust is the law set against such combinations.
normal.cn: 合起来，antitrust 就是针对这类联合的法律。

normal.en: Antitrust law forbids price fixing and market sharing.
normal.cn: antitrust law 禁止串通定价与瓜分市场。

normal.en: A trustbuster is the person or agency that enforces it.
normal.cn: trustbuster 就是执行这部法律的人或机构。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed on two boulders before they close into a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在两块巨石上，不让它们合成一堵墙。

abstract.en: Picture a referee standing between two merchants who want to split the street.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判站在两个想瓜分整条街的商人中间。

abstract.en: Picture a single stall forced to reopen as two competing stalls.
abstract.cn: 想象一个独占的摊位被拆成两个互相竞争的摊位。

examples.en: The two chains called off the deal after antitrust objections.
examples.cn: 在遭遇反垄断异议后，两家连锁企业取消了这笔交易。

examples.en: Antitrust authorities in three countries reviewed the same merger.
examples.cn: 三个国家的反垄断机构审查了同一桩合并。

examples.en: The court ordered an antitrust remedy that split the network in two.
examples.cn: 法院下令采取反垄断救济，把该网络一分为二。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「anti 加 trust」读起来像「安替托拉斯」——安一个替身去管住托拉斯；这只是拆词谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语前缀 anti-（反对）加英语 trust（托拉斯，企业巨头联合）：一八九〇年美国通过针对托拉斯的成文法，antitrust 由此成为一个固定的法律标签，核心义「反对企业联合限制竞争」。

sensesIntro.en: Antitrust starts as the law against restrictive combinations, keeps the historical colour of the trust campaign, then labels the enforcing agencies, the competitive effect, the academic field, and finally the break-up remedy.
sensesIntro.cn: antitrust 先指反对限制竞争联合的法律，保留反托拉斯运动的历史色彩，随后标注执法机构、竞争效果、学科领域，最后指拆分救济。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding two boulders apart so the market road stays open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把两块巨石分开，让市场通道保持通畅。

branches.en: The law against restraint of trade is the central sense.
branches.cn: 反对限制贸易的法律是中心义项。

branches.en: The historical campaign against the trusts is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 针对托拉斯的历史运动是最早的一层。

branches.en: Enforcement bodies and cases carry the law into practice.
branches.cn: 执法机构与案件把法律带入实践。

branches.en: The competitive effect is the purpose read as a description.
branches.cn: 竞争效果是把目的读成一种描述。

branches.en: The academic field and the break-up order are the two outer edges of the word.
branches.cn: 学科领域与拆分命令是这个词最外层的两个边缘。

intro.en: Antitrust is a two-part compound: the Greek prefix anti- and the noun trust, with English compounds such as trustbuster built on the same idea.
intro.cn: antitrust 是两段式复合词：希腊语前缀 anti- 加名词 trust，英语里还有 trustbuster 一类同想法的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix is Greek anti, against, borrowed into Latin; trust is not Latin at all but comes from Old Norse traust, help or confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀是希腊语 anti（反对），被拉丁语借用；trust 并非拉丁语，而来自古诺尔斯语 traust（援助、信心）。

items.example: Anti- is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: anti- 是复合词的前半。

items.example: Latin borrowed the Greek prefix and passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语借入这个希腊前缀，再传给英语。

items.example: Traust is the Norse source of trust.
items.exampleCN: traust 是 trust 的诺尔斯语来源。

items.meaning: confidence, and later a combined firm
items.example: The business sense of trust appears in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: trust 的商业义出现在十九世纪。

items.example: The adjective is fixed in law and policy.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在法律与政策里固定下来。

items.meaning: the statute and field of competition law
items.example: The compound names the whole body of rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指整套规则。

items.meaning: a person who breaks up trusts
items.example: The compound adds bust to trust.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在 trust 后加 bust。

items.example: The suffix -buster forms trustbuster.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -buster 构成 trustbuster。

items.meaning: the breaking up of large combinations
items.meaningCN: 反托拉斯行动；拆分垄断
items.example: The compound names the policy in plain words.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词用大白话指这项政策。

items.example: The parallel compound uses monopoly instead of trust.
items.exampleCN: 这个平行复合词用 monopoly 替换了 trust。

latinEntries.example: The prefix reached English through Latin compounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个前缀经拉丁语复合词进入英语。
